**Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 33, verse 32:**

*Aḥad* (أحد) originally means *waḥd* (one), and it is the "one." It was then used in general negation, where the masculine, the feminine, the singular, and what is beyond the singular are all equal. The meaning of His words ﴿You are not like any one of the women﴾ is: you are not like one group among the groups of women. That is, if you searched through the community of women group by group, you would not find a single group among them that equals you in merit and precedence. A similar example is His words, ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers, and make no distinction between any one of them﴾ [[Mahmud said: "Its meaning is 'you are not like one group among the groups of women,' that is, if you searched through the community of women group by group, you would not find among them a single group that equals you in merit and precedence. A similar example is: 'and make no distinction between any one of them.'" Ahmad said: What led him to make the comparison between the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the groups of women, rather than between their individuals, is that the comparands should correspond, because the first is a group. He had already been able to dispense with that by reading the statement as referring to one individual, and the meaning becomes more emphatic. The estimated sense is: "None of you is like any one of the women," that is, "like one of the women." It follows that if each of them is preferred over each individual woman, then their group is preferred over every group, but this does not follow in reverse. So consider this carefully, and Allah knows best. The comparison here comes in the same way as in His words, ﴿Is one who creates like one who does not create?﴾ and His words, ﴿And the male is not like the female﴾, in placing the more excellent first when making a comparison. A fine point has already been made about this, and Allah is the Granter of success.]]. He means among one group of them, as an equalizing of all of them in being upon the clear truth.

﴿If you fear Allah﴾: if you intend piety. [His words "and if you are pious women" (perhaps it is "or if," as in the wording of al-Nasafi). (ʿ)]

﴿Then do not be soft in speech﴾: do not speak with a yielding tone, that is, do not speak softly and languidly, like the speech of those who train (others) or of immoral women.

﴿So that one in whose heart is a disease may be moved to desire﴾: that is, doubt and lewdness.

It is also read in the jussive (*bi-l-jazm*), as a conjunction with the position of the verb of prohibition (*fiʿl al-nahy*, the prohibitive verb), on the basis that they were forbidden from being soft in speech. The one with a diseased heart is forbidden from desire, as if it were said: "Do not be soft, so that he does not desire."

It is reported from Ibn Muhaysin that he read it with a kasra on the *mīm* (فَيَطْمَعَ becoming فَيِطْمَعَ?). Its proper form is a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ* together with its kasra, and the verb is attributed to the pronoun of "speech," meaning: then the suspicious speech desires (the one in whose heart is a disease).

﴿Speak a good word﴾: far from the desire of the doubtful one, with seriousness and roughness, without softness; or "a good word" while being rough.

And ﴿wa-qarna﴾ is read with a kasra on the qaf, from waqara, yaqirru, waqaran. Alternatively it comes from qarra, yaqirru, where the first of the two identical letters (the ra') was dropped from the original *aqrarna*. Its kasra was moved onto the qaf, as one says *zulna* (from *dhalna*). *Qarna* with a fatha on the qaf is from the same root, and its original form was *aqrarna*. The ra' was dropped and its fatha was placed on the letter before it, as in your saying *zulna*. Abu al-Fath al-Hamdani mentioned another interpretation in his book *al-Tibyan*. He said: *qara yaqara* means "to gather together." From this comes *al-qarah* (the tribe of Qarah), because they gathered together. Do you not see the saying of ʿAdal and al-Daysh, the tribes: "Gather together and become a *qarah*"? [Footnote: The text "the saying of ʿAdal and al-Daysh" is in *al-Sihah*. There, "ʿAdal" is a tribe, namely ʿAdal ibn al-Hun ibn Khuzaymah, brother of al-Daysh. The two are the *qarah*. Also in it: "al-Daysh ibn al-Hun ibn Khuzaymah," and they sometimes say it with a fatha on the dal. He is one of the *qarah*, and the other is ʿAdal ibn al-Hun. Both together are called *al-qarah*. (ʿAyn, the abbreviation of the editor's note.)]

﴿al-jahiliyyah al-ula﴾ (the first jahiliyyah) is the ancient one, which is called "the utter jahiliyyah." It is the period in which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was born. Women wore pearl-woven garments and walked in the middle of the road, displaying themselves to men. It is also said that it lay between Adam and Nuh, or between Idris and Nuh, or in the time of Dawud and Sulayman. ﴿al-jahiliyyah al-ukhra﴾ (the other jahiliyyah) is the period between Isa and Muhammad (peace be upon them both). It is also permissible that the first jahiliyyah is the jahiliyyah of disbelief before Islam, and the other jahiliyyah is the jahiliyyah of wickedness and immorality within Islam. The meaning would then be: "Do not display yourselves in the manner of a jahiliyyah within Islam, imitating the people of the jahiliyyah of disbelief." This is supported by what is narrated: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him), "Indeed, there is jahiliyyah in you." He said, "Is it jahiliyyah of disbelief or of Islam?" He said, "Rather, it is jahiliyyah of disbelief." [Footnote: I did not find this from Abu al-Darda'; it is in the two Sahihs from Abu Dhar. It does not say "jahiliyyah of disbelief" ... to the end.]

He commanded them specifically regarding prayer and zakat, then brought the command generally to all acts of obedience. These two acts, the bodily and the financial, are the foundation of all other acts of obedience: whoever attends to them with full care is led by them to what lies beyond them. Then He stated that He forbade them, commanded them and admonished them only so that the People of the House of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not commit sins, and so that they would guard themselves against them through piety. He used the metaphor *rijs* (impurity) for sins, and *tuhr* (purity) for piety, because the honour of one who commits ugly deeds becomes soiled and defiled by them, just as his body becomes soiled by filth. As for the virtuous deeds, the honour with them is clean and protected, like a pure garment. In this metaphor there is something that repels people of intellect from what Allah has disliked for His servants and forbidden them, and encourages them toward what He is pleased with for them and commanded them.

﴿Ahla al-bayt﴾ (the People of the House) is in the accusative as a vocative (an address), or as a praise. This is clear evidence that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are among his household (ahl al-bayt).

Then He mentioned that their houses are the descent-places of revelation, and commanded them not to forget what is recited in them of the Book, which combines two matters: it is clear signs that testify to the truth of prophethood, since it is a miracle by its composition; and it is wisdom, sciences, and laws. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle, Acquainted﴾, when He knew what benefits you and sets right your religion, so He sent it down to you.

Or [it means]: He knew who is fit for His prophethood and who is fit to be the people of his household. Or [it means]: when He made one single speech combine the two aims.

It is narrated that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Messenger of God, God has mentioned the men in the Qur'an with goodness. Is there no good in us by which we might be mentioned? We fear that our obedience is not accepted." [[Narrated by al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh from the transmission of Ibn Zabyan from Ibn Abbas: "The women said: 'O Messenger of God, why are we not mentioned in the Qur'an?' ... the hadith."]] It is also said that the one who asked was Umm Salama. [[Narrated by al-Nasa'i from the transmission of Shurayk from Muhammad ibn Umar from Abu Salama from Umm Salama, who said: "O Messenger of God, why do I hear the men being mentioned in the Qur'an, while the women are not mentioned?" So God, exalted is He, revealed ﴿Indeed the men who submit and the women who submit﴾ and the verse. It was also narrated by al-Tabarani and al-Tabari from another route from Muhammad ibn Umar. Ahmad, Ibn Rahawayh and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the transmission of Uthman ibn Hakim from Abd al-Rahman ibn Shayba from Umm Salama. al-Hakim narrated it through the route of Mujahid from Umm Salama, and al-Tirmidhi narrated a similar report from Umm Umara.]]

It is also narrated that when what was revealed about the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) was revealed, the women of the Muslims said: "Has nothing been revealed about us?" [[Narrated by al-Tabari from the transmission of Sa'id from Qatada, who said: "Some believing women entered upon the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'We have been mentioned in the Qur'an...' the hadith." Ibn Sa'd narrated it from al-Waqidi from Ma'mar from Qatada.]] Then it was revealed.

Al-muslim (the one who submits): one who enters into peace (salm) after war, the one who yields and does not resist; or one who entrusts his affair to God, relying upon Him, one who has surrendered his face to God. Al-mu'min (the believer): one who affirms God and His Messenger and what must be affirmed.

Al-qanit (the devout one): one who stands in obedience and constantly persists in it. Al-sadiq (the truthful one): one who is truthful in his intention, speech and deeds. Al-sabir (the patient one): one who is patient in acts of obedience and in refraining from acts of disobedience. Al-khashi' (the humble one): one who is humble before God with his heart and his limbs. It is also said: one who, when he prays, does not notice who is on his right or left. Al-mutasaddiq (the almsgiver): one who gives the zakat on his wealth and does not neglect the voluntary acts (nawafil, supererogatory acts). It is also said: whoever gives a dirham in charity in a week is among the almsgivers. And whoever fasts the white days (al-bid) of every month is among those who fast.

Al-dhakir Allah kathiran (the one who remembers God much): one who is almost never free of the remembrance of God, with his heart, his tongue, or both. Reciting the Qur'an and occupying oneself with knowledge are both forms of remembrance. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever awakens from his sleep and wakes his wife, and they both pray two rak'ahs together, they are written among the men and women who remember God much." [[Narrated by the authors of the Sunan, except al-Tirmidhi, from the transmission of al-Aghar from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayra, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).]]

The meaning is: "and the women who guard them (al-hafizat ha) and the women who remember Him (al-dhakirat)," and it is elided because the apparent meaning indicates it. If you ask: what is the difference between the two conjunctions, namely the conjunction of the feminine over the masculine, and the conjunction of the pair over the pair? I say: the first conjunction is like God's words ﴿previously married and virgins﴾ in that the two are different genera; when they share a ruling, there must be a conjunction (waw) placed between them. As for the second conjunction, it is the conjunction of an attribute over an attribute with the plural particle, so its meaning is as if it were: "Indeed, the men and women who combine these acts of obedience, ﴿God has prepared for them﴾..."

Zamakhshari's Commentary (al-Kashshaf) on Surah 33, verse 36:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed Zaynab bint Jahsh, the daughter of his paternal aunt Umayma bint Abd al-Muttalib, to his freed slave Zayd ibn Haritha. She refused, and her brother Abd Allah refused too. Then the verse was revealed, and they said: "We accept, O Messenger of Allah." So he married her to him, and he paid on his behalf her dowry: sixty dirhams, a head-covering (khimar), a wrapper (milhafa), a shirt (dir'), a waist-wrap (izar), fifty mudd of food, and thirty sa' of dates. [[I have not found it with a complete chain. Its opening is in al-Daraqutni, through the narration of al-Kumayt ibn Zayd al-Asadi the poet, from Madhkur ibn Zayd al-Asadi, the mawla of Zaynab bint Jahsh, from Zaynab bint Jahsh, who said: "Several men of Quraysh proposed to me. My sister Hamna sent someone to consult the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said to her: 'Where is she in regard to her husband?'" - the hadith continues - and its isnad is weak.

It does not mention the amount of the dowry. However, Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted it from Muqatil ibn Hayyan as a statement of a Successor (maqtu').]] 

It is also said that she was Umm Kulthum bint Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt, who was the first woman to emigrate, and who gave herself in marriage to the Prophet (ﷺ). He said: "I have accepted," and he married her to Zayd.

She and her brother were displeased and said: "We only wanted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he married us to his slave." [[al-Tha'labi related it in this form without a chain. al-Tabari related from the narration of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam that this was his own statement.]]

The meaning: "It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter (idha qada Allah wa rasuluhu amran), that they should have any choice in their affair" - that is, the Messenger of Allah, or because the decision of the Messenger of Allah is the decision of Allah. Rather, it is their duty to make their opinion follow his opinion, and their choice follow his choice.

If you say: "The pronoun should have been singular, as you would say: 'No man or woman came to me except that such-and-such was his affair.'" I say: Yes, but since they both fell under the negation, it is as if it had said "every believing man and woman," so the pronoun refers to the meaning and not to the wording.

It has been read as yakun, with a ta' and with a ya'. And al-Khiyara (choice) is what is chosen.

لِلَّذِي أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ بالإسلام الذي هو أجل النعم، وبتوفيقك لعتقه ومحبته واختصاصه ﴿الَّذِي أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ﴾ ﴿وَأَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ بما وفقك الله فيه، فهو متقلب في نعمة الله ونعمة رسوله ﷺ، وهو زيد بن حارثة. ﴿أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ﴾ يعني زينب بنت جحش رضي الله عنها، وذلك أن رسول الله ﷺ أبصرها بعد ما أنكحها إياه، فوقعت في نفسه، فقال: «سبحان الله مقلب القلوب»، وذلك أنّ نفسه كانت تجفو عنها قبل ذلك لا تريدها، ولو أرادتها لاختطبها، وسمعت زينب بالتسبيحة فذكرتها لزيد، ففطن وألقى الله في نفسه كراهة صحبتها والرغبة عنها لرسول الله ﷺ، فقال لرسول الله ﷺ: إني أريد أن أفارق صاحبتي، فقال: «مالك؟ أرابك منها شيء؟» قال: لا والله، ما رأيت منها إلا خيرا، ولكنها تتعظم عليّ لشرفها وتؤذيني، فقال له: «أمسك عليك زوجك واتق الله»، ثم طلقها بعد، فلما اعتدت قال رسول الله ﷺ: «ما أجد أحدا أوثق في نفسي منك، اخطب عليّ زينب». قال زيد: فانطلقت فإذا هي تخمر عجينتها، فلما رأيتها عظمت في صدري حتى ما أستطيع أن أنظر إليها، حين علمت أنّ رسول الله ﷺ ذكرها، فوليتها ظهري وقلت: يا زينب، أبشري إنّ رسول الله ﷺ يخطبك، ففرحت وقالت: ما أنا بصانعة شيئا حتى أؤامر ربي، فقامت إلى مسجدها، ونزل القرآن [[ذكره الثعلبي بغير سند. وأخرج الطبري معناه من رواية عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم قوله، وفي الصحيحين عن أنس قصة زينب وزيد مختصرة. وليس فيه مما في أوله.]] ﴿زَوَّجْناكَها﴾ فتزوجها رسول الله ﷺ ودخل بها، وما أولم على امرأة من نسائه ما أولم عليها: ذبح شاة وأطعم الناس الخبز واللحم حتى امتد النهار.

فإن قلت: ما أراد بقوله ﴿وَاتَّقِ اللَّهَ﴾؟ قلت: أراد: واتق الله فلا تطلقها، وقصد نهي تنزيه لا تحريم، لأن الأولى أن لا يطلق. وقيل: أراد: واتق الله فلا تذمّها بالنسبة إلى الكبر وأذى الزوج.

فإن قلت: ما الذي أخفى في نفسه؟ قلت: تعلق قلبه بها.

وقيل: مودة مفارقة زيد إياها. وقيل: علمه بأن زيدا سيطلقها وسينكحها، لأن الله قد أعلمه بذلك. وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها: «لو كتم رسول الله ﷺ شيئا مما أوحي إليه لكتم هذه الآية» [[متفق عليه من حديث عائشة رضي الله عنها.]].

فإن قلت: فماذا أراد الله منه أن يقوله حين قال له زيد: أريد مفارقتها، وكان من الهجنة أن يقول له: افعل، فإني أريد نكاحها؟ قلت: كأن الذي أراد منه عز وجل أن يصمت عند ذلك، أو يقول له: أنت أعلم بشأنك، حتى لا يخالف سره في ذلك علانيته، لأن الله يريد من الأنبياء تساوي الظاهر والباطن، والتصلب في الأمور، والتجاوب في الأحوال، والاستمرار على طريقة مستتبة، كما جاء في حديث إرادة رسول الله ﷺ قتل عبد الله بن أبي سرح واعتراض عثمان بشفاعته له: أن عمر قال له: «لقد كان عيني إلى عينك، هل تشير إليّ فأقتله؟» فقال: «إن الأنبياء لا تومض، [[قوله «لا تومض» في الصحاح: أومضت المرأة، إذا سارقت النظر. (ع)]] ظاهرهم وباطنهم واحد» [[لم أجده، وفي الدلائل للبيهقي من رواية الحسن بن بشر عن الحكم بن عبد الملك عن قتادة عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: «أمن رسول الله ﷺ الناس يوم فتح مكة إلا أربعة من الناس» - فذكر الحديث - قال: «ونذر رجل من الأنصار أن يقتل عبد الله بن سعد إذا رآه، فأتى به عثمان فشفع له، فجعل الأنصاري يتردد ويكره أن يقدم عليه. فبايعه النبي ﷺ ثم قال للأنصاري: قد انتظرتك. قال: يا رسول الله أفلا أرمضت إليّ؟ قال: إنه ليس للنبي أن يومض». وأخرجه الطبري من رواية سعيد عن قتادة مرسلا. وروى عبد الرزاق من طريق مقسم مولى ابن عباس قال: «لما كانت المدة بين رسول الله ﷺ وبين قريش» - فذكر الحديث بطوله وفيه: «وأمن الناس إلا أربعة». وفيه: فجاء عثمان بابن أبي سرح. فقال: بايعه يا رسول الله، فأعرض عنه ثم جاء فبايعه، فقال: لقد أعرضت عنه ليقتله بعضكم، فقال رجل من الأنصار: هلا أومضت إلينا يا رسول الله؟ قال: إن النبي لا يومض». وهذا مرسل أيضا، وأخرجه أبو داود وغيره من حديث سعد بن أبي وقاص نحو الأول، لكن في آخره: «ثم أقبل على أصحابه فقال: أفما كان فيكم رجل رشيد، يقوم إلى هذا حيث رآني كففت يدي عنه فيقتله؟ قالوا: وما يدرينا يا رسول الله ما في نفسك، هلا أومأت إلينا بعينك؟ قال: لا ينبغي لنبي أن يكون له خائنة الأعين».]].

فإن قلت: كيف عاتبه الله في ستر ما استهجن التصريح به، ولا يستهجن النبيّ ﷺ التصريح بشيء إلا والشيء في نفسه مستهجن، وقالة الناس لا تتعلق إلا بما يستقبح في العقول والعادات؟ وما له لم يعاتبه في نفس الأمر ولم يأمره بقمع الشهوة وكف النفس عن أن تنازع إلى زينب وتتبعها؟ ولم يعصم نبيه ﷺ عن تعلق الهجنة به وما يعرضه للقالة؟

قلت: كم من شيء يتحفظ منه الإنسان ويستحيي من اطلاع الناس عليه، وهو في نفسه مباح متسع، وحلال مطلق، لا مقال فيه ولا عيب عند الله، وربما كان الدخول في ذلك المباح سلما إلى حصول واجبات يعظم أثرها في الدين ويجل ثوابها، ولو لم يتحفظ منه لأطلق كثير من الناس فيه ألسنتهم إلا من أوتي فضلا وعلما ودينا ونظرا في حقائق الأمور ولبوبها دون قشورها. ألا ترى أنهم كانوا إذا طمعوا في بيوت رسول الله ﷺ بقوا مرتكزين في مجالسهم لا يريمون مستأنسين بالحديث، وكان رسول الله ﷺ يؤذيه قعودهم ويضيق صدره حديثهم، والحياء يصده أن يأمرهم بالانتشار، حتى نزلت ﴿إِنَّ ذلِكُمْ كانَ يُؤْذِي النَّبِيَّ فَيَسْتَحْيِي مِنْكُمْ وَاللَّهُ لا يَسْتَحْيِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ﴾. ولو أبرز رسول الله ﷺ مكنون ضميره وأمرهم أن ينتشروا، لشق عليهم، ولكان بعض المقالة، [[قوله «ولكان بعض المقالة» لعله: القالة. (ع)]] فهذا من ذاك القبيل، لأن طموح قلب الإنسان إلى بعض مشتهياته من امرأة أو غيرها غير موصوف بالقبح في العقل ولا في الشرع، لأنه ليس بفعل الإنسان ولا وجوده باختياره، وتناول المباح بالطريق الشرعي ليس بقبيح أيضا، وهو خطبة زينب ونكاحها من غير استنزال زيد عنها، ولا طلب إليه وهو أقرب منه من زر قميصه أن يواسيه بمفارقتها، مع قوة العلم بأن نفس زيد لم تكن من التعلق بها في شيء، بل كانت تجفو عنها، ونفس رسول الله ﷺ متعلقة بها، ولم يكن مستنكرا عندهم أن ينزل الرجل عن امرأته لصديقه، ولا مستهجنا إذا نزل عنها أن ينكحها الآخر، فإنّ المهاجرين حين دخلوا المدينة استهم الأنصار بكل شيء، حتى إن الرجل منهم إذا كانت له امرأتان نزل عن إحداهما وأنكحها المهاجر، وإذا كان الأمر مباحا من جميع جهاته ولم يكن فيه وجه من وجوه القبح ولا مفسدة ولا مضرة بزيد ولا بأحد، بل كان مستجرا مصالح، ناهيك بواحدة منها أن بنت عمة رسول الله ﷺ أمنت الأيمة والضيعة ونالت الشرف وعادت أما من أمهات المسلمين. إلى ما ذكر الله عز وجل من المصلحة العامة في قوله ﴿لِكَيْ لا يَكُونَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ حَرَجٌ فِي أَزْواجِ أَدْعِيائِهِمْ إِذا قَضَوْا مِنْهُنَّ وَطَراً﴾، فبالحرى أن يعاتب الله رسوله حين كتمه وبالغ في كتمه بقوله ﴿أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ وَاتَّقِ اللَّهَ﴾، وأن لا يرضى له إلا اتحاد الضمير والظاهر، والثبات في مواطن الحق، حتى يقتدي به المؤمنون فلا يستحيوا من المكافحة بالحق وإن كان مرا.

فإن قلت: الواو في ﴿وَتُخْفِي فِي نَفْسِكَ، وَتَخْشَى النَّاسَ وَاللَّهُ أَحَقُّ﴾ ما هي؟ قلت: واو الحال، أي: تقول لزيد: أمسك عليك زوجك مخفيا في نفسك إرادة أن لا يمسكها، وتخفي خاشيا قالة الناس، وتخشى الناس، حقيقا في ذلك بأن تخشى الله، أو واو العطف، كأنه قيل: وإذ تجمع بين قولك: أمسك، وإخفاء خلافه، وخشية الناس، والله أحق أن تخشاه، حتى لا تفعل مثل ذلك.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 33, verse 40:

﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾, meaning: he was not the father of any man among you in actuality, such that there would be established between him and them what is established between a father and his child, such as the prohibition of marriage by affinity and the bond of marriage. ﴿But he is the Messenger of Allah﴾, and every messenger is a father to his nation in what pertains to the obligation of honoring and revering him on their part, and the obligation of compassion and sincere counsel to them on his part, but not in the other rulings that are established between fathers and sons. Zayd was one of your men who was not his child in actuality, so his ruling was your ruling, and the claim of sonship and adoption is only a matter of special closeness and nearness, nothing more. ﴿And the Seal of the Prophets﴾, meaning: if he had had a son who reached the age of men, that son would have been a prophet, and he would not have been the Seal of the Prophets, as is narrated that he said about Ibrahim when he died: "If he had lived, he would have been a prophet"[[Narrated by Ibn Majah through the chain of Muqsim from Ibn Abbas in the course of a hadith. And in al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Ibn Abi Awfa: "If it had been decreed that there would be a prophet after Muhammad, his son would have lived, but there is no prophet after him."]]. If you say: Was he not the father of al-Tayyib, al-Tahir, al-Qasim and Ibrahim? I say: they were excluded from the scope of the negation by His words ﴿of your men﴾ in two respects. One: these did not reach the age of men. The second: He attributed "men" to them, and these were his men, not their men. If you say: Was he not the father of al-Hasan and al-Husayn? I say: Yes, but they were not men at that time, and they were also among his men, not among their men. And there is another matter: he intended only his own son specifically, not the son of his son, due to His words ﴿and the Seal of the Prophets﴾. Do you not see that al-Hasan and al-Husayn lived until one of them exceeded forty and the other fifty?[[His words "nayyafa ahaduhuma" mean: exceeded. Al-nayf, with doubled or single fa', means excess, as in al-Sihah. (Ayn)]]

It was read: ﴿But the Messenger of Allah﴾ in the accusative, in coordination with ﴿father of any one﴾; and in the nominative, meaning: "But he is the Messenger of Allah." And "lakinna" with the shadda, with the predicate omitted, its estimate being: "But the Messenger of Allah is the one you know," meaning: no male son lived for him. "Khatam" with a fatha on the ta' means the stamp, and with a kasra it means the stamp and also the agent of sealing. The reading of Ibn Mas'ud supports this: "But a prophet, the seal of the prophets." If you say: How could he be the last of the prophets when Jesus is to descend at the end of time? I say: the meaning of his being the last of the prophets is that no one will be given prophethood after him, and Jesus was given prophethood before him, and when he descends he will descend acting upon the law of Muhammad, facing his qibla, as if he were part of his nation.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 33, verses 41–42:

﴿Remember Allah with much remembrance﴾: praise Him with the various kinds of praise, such as declaring Him free of imperfection (taqdis), praising Him (tahmid), declaring His oneness (tahlil), and magnifying Him (takbir), and with whatever is befitting of Him, and do this often, ﴿morning and evening﴾: that is, at all times.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The remembrance of Allah is on the tongue of every Muslim" [[I have not found it with this wording. al-Daraqutni and al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Adi narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: "A man asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'One of us slaughters and forgets to mention the name [of Allah]?' He said: 'The name of Allah is on the tongue of every Muslim.'" Among its narrators is Marwan ibn Salim.

And he is very weak.]]. And it was narrated: "in the heart of every Muslim." And from Qatadah: "Say: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-Ali al-Azim." And from Mujahid: "These are words that the pure person and the one in a state of major impurity (junub) say."

The two verbs, I mean "remember" (udhkuru) and "glorify" (sabbihu), are directed at "morning and evening," as when you say: "Fast and pray on Friday." Glorification (tasbih) is part of remembrance (dhikr), but He singled it out from among its kinds in the way Jibril and Mikail are singled out from among the angels, to show its excellence over the other forms of remembrance, because its meaning is declaring His essence free of what is impermissible for Him of attributes and actions, and clearing Him of blemishes. An example of its excellence over other forms of remembrance is the excellence of describing a servant as pure from the filth of sins and clean from the defilements of wrongdoing, over all his other qualities such as much prayer and fasting, devotion to all acts of obedience, engagement in knowledge, and renown for virtues.

It is also permissible that by remembrance and its abundance He means: increasing acts of obedience and devoting oneself to acts of worship, for every act of obedience and every good is part of remembrance. Then He singled out glorification from that, "morning and evening," meaning the prayer at all its times, because of the excellence of prayer over other things. Or it means the Fajr prayer and the two evening prayers (al-Isha'ayn), because their performance is more difficult and their observance more demanding.

The Qur'an verse 43-44 commentary, from al-Zamakhshari's *al-Kashshaf*:

Since bowing and prostration in prayer (salat) involve inclining, the word was borrowed for one who inclines toward another out of tenderness and compassion, like a visitor of a sick person who bends over him, or a mother's tenderness toward her child. Then its use spread until it was applied to mercy and compassion. From this is the saying "ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayka," meaning "may Allah have mercy on you and be compassionate toward you." If you say: "His saying, ﴿He it is who sends blessings upon you﴾, if you interpret it as 'he shows mercy to you and is compassionate toward you' [[Mahmud said: 'If you take yuṣallī (sends blessings) to mean yarḥam (shows mercy), then what about the angels' sending blessings along with Him?' He answered that since the angels ask Allah for mercy and He answers their supplication with it, they were treated as if they were the ones doing the mercy, just as you say: 'ḥayyāka Allāh' (may Allah give you life), meaning 'aḥyāka' (He gives you life), and then you say: 'ḥayyaytuhu' (I gave him life), meaning 'I asked Allah to give him life.' The purpose of that is to make life certain for him, as if you said: 'I asked Allah for life for him, and the supplication was answered.'' Aḥmad said: 'Al-Zamakhshari often avoids believing that a single word is meant in both its literal and figurative senses at once, and he has committed to it here. But he made the prayer from Allah literal and from the angels figurative, because he understood it as mercy. Others understood it as supplication, and made it literal for the angels and figurative for Allah. And Allah knows best.']], then what do you do with His saying ﴿and His angels﴾? And what is the meaning of their blessing?" I say: it is their saying, "O Allah, bless the believers." Because they are those whose supplications are answered, they were treated as if they were the ones doing the mercy and compassion. A parallel is His saying: "ḥayyāka Allāh," meaning "aḥyāka wa-abqāka" (may Allah give you life and keep you), and "ḥayyaytuka," meaning "I prayed for you that Allah give you life." Since you rely on the answer to your supplication, it is as if you were giving him life in reality. Likewise "ʿammaraka Allāh" and "ʿammartuka," and "saqāka Allāh" and "saqaytuka." On this basis is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him﴾, meaning: ask Allah to bless him. The meaning is: He it is who shows mercy to you and is compassionate toward you, in that He calls you to goodness and commands you to remember Him often and to devote yourselves to prayer and obedience, ﴿that He may bring you out from the darknesses into the light﴾ of obedience, ﴿and ever is He, toward the believers, Merciful﴾. This is evidence that the intended meaning of ṣalāt here is mercy.

It is narrated that when His saying was revealed, ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾, Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have not been singled out for any honour except that we have been given a share in it." So the verse was revealed: ﴿Their greeting﴾. The phrase is an idafa of the verbal noun to its object: on the day they meet Him they are greeted with peace. It is possible that Allah honours them by greeting them with peace, as He treats them with every other kind of honour. It may also be a metaphor like "liqāʾ" (meeting), as we explained. It was said: it is the greeting of the Angel of Death and the angels with him to them, and their good news of Paradise. It was said: it is the greeting of the angels at the moment of leaving the graves. It was said: it is at the entering of Paradise, as He says: ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate: "Peace be upon you"﴾. ﴿A generous reward﴾ is Paradise.

Witness over those to whom you were sent, and over their denial and their affirmation; that is, your word will be accepted by God concerning them and against them, just as the word of a just witness is accepted in judgment. If you say: how was he a witness at the time of sending, when witness is only one who bears testimony at the time of taking it or at the time of giving it? I reply: this is a circumstantial clause of anticipation (hal muqaddarah), like the example in the Book: "I passed by a man with a falcon, hunting with it tomorrow," meaning: one intending to hunt with it tomorrow. If you say: from His saying "Indeed We have sent you as a caller" it is already understood that he is permitted to call, so what is the benefit of His saying "by His permission"? I reply: it does not mean literal permission; rather, "permission" is used figuratively for facilitation and ease, because entering upon the right of the owner is difficult, but when permission is met, it becomes easy and smooth. So when permission was facilitation for what is otherwise difficult, it was placed in its position. This is because calling the people of polytheism and the age of ignorance to monotheism and the sacred laws is a matter of extreme difficulty and hardship. Therefore it was said "by His permission," to signal that the matter is hard, cannot be achieved and cannot be undertaken except when God makes it easy and smooth. From this is their saying about the miser: he is not permitted to spend, that is, it is not facilitated for him to spend, because it is burdensome to him and falls under the category of the difficult. Through him God made clear the darkness of polytheism, and those who had gone astray were guided by him, just as the darkness of night is illuminated by a shining lamp and guided by it. Or: God extended, by the light of His prophethood, the light of insights, just as by the light of a lamp the light of eyes is extended. He described it as illuminating because among lamps there are those that do not give light when their oil is scant and their wick is fine. In the words of some: three things give light: a slow messenger, a lamp that does not shine, and a table for which one awaits a guest to come. Someone was asked about the lonely, and he said: a concealing darkness and a faint lamp. It was also said: "and a shining lamp" (read as wa-dhā sirājan munīran), or "and a reciter, a shining lamp" (wa-tāliyan sirājan munīran). According to this interpretation, it is permissible to conjoin it to the kaf in "We have sent you."

I reply: it does not mean literal permission; rather, "permission" is used figuratively for facilitation and ease, because entering upon the right of the owner is difficult, but when permission is met, it becomes easy and smooth. So when permission was facilitation for what is otherwise difficult, it was placed in its position. This is because calling the people of polytheism and the age of ignorance to monotheism and the sacred laws is a matter of extreme difficulty and hardship. Therefore it was said "by His permission," to signal that the matter is hard, cannot be achieved and cannot be undertaken except when God makes it easy and smooth. From this is their saying about the miser: he is not permitted to spend, that is, it is not facilitated for him to spend, because it is burdensome to him and falls under the category of the difficult. Through him God made clear the darkness of polytheism, and those who had gone astray were guided by him, just as the darkness of night is illuminated by a shining lamp and guided by it. Or: God extended, by the light of His prophethood, the light of insights, just as by the light of a lamp the light of eyes is extended. He described it as illuminating because among lamps there are those that do not give light when their oil is scant and their wick is fine. In the words of some: three things give light: a slow messenger, a lamp that does not shine, and a table for which one awaits a guest to come. Someone was asked about the lonely, and he said: a concealing darkness and a faint lamp. It was also said: "and a shining lamp" (read as wa-dhā sirājan munīran), or "and a reciter, a shining lamp" (wa-tāliyan sirājan munīran). According to this interpretation, it is permissible to conjoin it to the kaf in "We have sent you."

Al-Fadl: what He bestows upon them beyond the reward. When the bestowal is mentioned and described as great, then consider what the reward must be. It is also permissible that by al-fadl He means the reward, from the expression used for gifts: fudul and fawaʼid (surplus gifts). And it is also permissible that He means they have a great favour (fadl kabir) over the rest of the nations, and that this favour is from God, and that He gave them what made them superior.

This is Qur'anic text with the rest a commentary. Translating faithfully.

"And do not obey the disbelievers" — its meaning: persistence and steadiness upon what he was already doing. Or it is an incitement (not to yield to them). "Their harm" (adhahum) may be construed as an idafa (possessive construction) to the agent or to the patient. That is: leave off harming them with injury or killing, take their outward profession at face value, and let their inward state be their reckoning with God. Or: leave off what they inflict upon you by way of harm, and do not requite them for it until you are commanded to. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that this verse was abrogated (mansukha) by the verse of the sword. "And rely upon Allah, for He suffices as a guardian (wakil)" — and sufficient is He as one to whom affairs are entrusted.

It may be said: God described him with five attributes and paired each of them with an address suited to it. He paired the witness (shahid), by His words "and give good tidings to the believers," because he is a witness over his community, and they are witnesses over all the other nations; this is the great virtue. He paired the bearer of good tidings (mubashshir) with turning away from the disbelievers and hypocrites, because when he turns away from them he gives his full attention entirely to the believers, which accords with good tidings. He paired the warner (nadhir) with leaving off their harm, because if he leaves off harming them in the present—and harm must have a punishment, either swift or delayed—they will be warned of it in the future. He paired the one who summons to Allah (da'i ila Allah) with making it easy for him, by His words "and rely upon Allah," because whoever relies upon Allah, every difficulty is made easy for him. He paired the illuminating lamp (siraj munir) with being sufficed by Him as guardian, because whom Allah has illuminated with a proof over all His creation is worthy of being sufficed by Him over all His creation.

Al-Nikah (نكاح): intercourse (الوطء), and calling the contract "nikah" is a metonymy because it is the means to intercourse. A parallel is calling wine "sin" (إثم), because it causes the committing of sin. In the science of rhetoric (علم البيان, 'ilm al-bayan) there is a similar line by the rajaz poet:

*Humps of camels in its clouds,*
*It came forward like one that prances, from its Rabab (clouds),*
*As if the heavy rain were in its striking.*

"Humps of camels in its clouds" describes rain as abundant and plentiful. It is said: istanna al-faras (استن الفرس), when the horse kicked and played, which is to raise its forelegs and drop them at times and its hind legs at other times in succession. Qamisa al-bahr bil-safina (قمص البحر بالسفينة) means the sea made the ship move, raising its prow at one time and its stern at another. So al-mustann (المستن) is the active participle of this verb, used as a metaphor for the cloud when it comes forward moving and containing rain. Al-Rabab means white clouds packed tightly together. The pronoun in "aqbala" (أقبل) and "rababihi" (ربابه) refers to the rain. Al-Wabil (الوابل) is an explicit noun placed in the position of a pronoun, to indicate abundance. "Fi mus'abihi" (في مصابه) is a circumstantial clause (حال) for it. "Asnimat al-aabal" (أسنمة الآبال) is the subject (مبتدأ), "fi sahabihi" (في سحابه) is the predicate (خبر), and the whole clause is the predicate of al-wabil. He applied the term "humps" (أسنمة) to the water because it is the cause of the fattening of camels. Al-Musab is a verbal noun (مصدر) in the form of a passive participle. Al-Wabil means heavy, strongly striking rain. Al-Asnima is the plural of sanam (سنام, hump). Al-Aabal, with the hamza lengthened, is the plural of ibl (إبل, camels).

He named the water "humps of camels" because it is the cause of the fatness of wealth and the rising of its humps. The word nikah (نكاح) does not occur in the Book of Allah except with the meaning of the contract, because in the sense of intercourse it is stated explicitly. Among the etiquettes of the Qur'an is that intercourse is alluded to with words such as mulamasa (ملامسة, touching), mumassa (مماسة, touching), qurban (قربان, approaching), taghshi (تغشّي, covering) and ityan (إتيان, coming to). 

If you ask: why did He specify "the believing women" when the ruling in the verse applies equally to believing and People of the Book women? I answer: specifying them alerts that the basic principle, and what is better for the believer, is that he choose for his offspring, and that he marry only a believing, chaste woman, and keep away from marrying sinners, let alone disbelievers, and that he disdain to lie under one blanket with an enemy of Allah and His friend. The verse in Surat al-Ma'ida (تعليم ما هو جائز غير محرّم) teaches what is permissible and not forbidden, namely marrying the chaste women of those who were given the Book. This verse teaches what is better for the believers: marrying believing women.

If you ask: what is the purpose of "thumma" (ثم) in His saying, ﴿then you divorce them﴾? I answer: its purpose is to negate the suspicion in one who may think the ruling differs between divorcing her when she is recently married, and divorcing her after a long time has passed in the bond of marriage. If you ask: if he is alone with her in a valid privacy in which touching is possible, does that take the place of touching? I answer: yes, according to Abu Hanifa and his companions, a valid privacy (خلوة صحيحة) has the ruling of touching. His saying ﴿so you have no waiting period for them which you should count﴾ is evidence that the waiting period is a right owed by women to men. "Ta'taddunaha" (تعتدونها) means you complete its count, from your saying: 'addtu al-darahim fa-i'taddaha (عددت الدراهم فاعتدها), like your saying: kiltuhu fa-iktaluhu (كلته فأكتاله) and wazanahu fa-itazanahu (وزنته فاتزنه). It is also read as "ta'tadunaha" with a lightened letter, meaning you act with transgression in it, like the verse of the poet:

[The verse is cited here by the author; the poem's line is recorded in the source, and its explanation was given in volume two, page 408, so refer to it if you wish.]

The meaning of i'tida' (اعتداد, reckoning) is what is in His saying: ﴿and do not keep them in marriage to harm them, to transgress﴾. If you ask: is this provision (التمتيع, tamti') obligatory or recommended? I answer: if she was not assigned a dower, the provision is obligatory, and according to Abu Hanifa it is obligatory only for her alone, not for the rest of the divorced women. If she was assigned a dower, the provision is disputed: some hold it is recommended and desirable, and among them is Abu Hanifa; others hold it is obligatory. ﴿A fair release﴾ means without harm or withholding, which is obligatory.

ʾujūrahunna (their dowries): the mahr, since the mahr is a compensation (ajr) for intimacy (al-bud'). Wa-itā'uhā (and giving them): either handing them over promptly, or fixing the amount and naming it in the contract. Fa-in qult: why did He say "those whom you have given their dowries" and "of what God has granted you as spoils" and "those who emigrated with you," and what is the benefit of these specifications? I say: God chose for His Messenger the most excellent and preferable, and favoured him with the purest and most pure-hearted, just as He singled him out with other special privileges, and gave him precedence over others with such distinction. That is because naming the mahr in the contract is preferable and more excellent than leaving it unnamed, though the contract remains valid; and he may consummate the marriage, and then the woman is owed the mahr al-mithl (the customary dowry) if he has consummated with her, and a mut'ah (provision) if he has not. Bringing the mahr to her promptly is better than naming it and deferring it; and prompt payment was the practice (ditan) and custom (sunnah) of the early generations (al-salaf), and nothing else was known among them. Likewise a slave-woman whose owner is her master, and [the spoils of] his sword and lance, and what God has taken as booty from the territory of war is more lawful and pure than what is bought from the market of the caravan-sellers (shiqq al-jalab). Captives are of two kinds: the good captive (sabi tayyiba) and the foul captive (sabi khabitha). The good captive is what is taken from the people of war; but whoever has a covenant (ʿahd), those taken from them are a foul captive. This is indicated by His words, "of what God has granted you as spoils (fay')," because the term fay' of God is applied only to the good and not to the foul, just as the term rizq of God must be applied only to the lawful and not to the unlawful. [Note: his saying "just as the provision of God must be applied only to the lawful" is the view of the Mu'tazilah. As for the People of the Sunnah, they apply it to both categories. (ʿA)] Likewise, those of his paternal cousins (qarāʾib) who emigrated with the Messenger of God ﷺ, who are not forbidden to him (ghayr al-maḥārim), are more excellent than the women who did not emigrate with him. From Umm Hani bint Abi Talib: "The Messenger of God ﷺ proposed to me, and I excused myself to him, and he accepted my excuse. Then God revealed this verse, and I was not lawful to him, because I had not emigrated with him; I was among the freed ones (al-Tulaqa')." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, al-Hakim, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ishaq, al-Tabari, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Abi Hatim, all through the narration of al-Suddi from Abu Salih from her.]

"And We have made lawful to you the women who offer themselves to you (in gift) if the Prophet wishes to marry them, (and) a believing woman who gives herself to the Prophet; this is only for you, not for the (rest of) believers." This applies if such an occurrence happens; and that is why it is stated in indefinite form (nakkara). There is disagreement about whether such an occurrence actually took place. From Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: "None of them was in the Prophet's ﷺ possession by way of gift." It is said the women who gave themselves were four: Maymunah bint al-Harith, Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, mother of the poor, the Ansari woman, Umm Sharik bint Jabir, and Khawlah bint Hakim, may God be pleased with them all. It is read "in in wahabat" (if she gives herself) as a conditional. al-Hasan read "in" with a fatha, as a causal clause with the lam elided. It may also be a verbal noun (masdar) with the time element omitted, as in your saying: "Sit as long as Zayd is sitting," meaning the time of his continuing to sit, and the time of her giving herself. Ibn Mas'ud read it without "an." If you ask: what is the meaning of the second condition together with the first? I say: it restricts the first; the condition for the lawfulness is her gifting herself, and in the gift there is the intent that the Messenger of God ﷺ wishes to marry her in full; as if he said: "We have made her lawful to you if she gives herself to you and you wish to take her in marriage," because his wish is the acceptance of the gift and what completes it. If you ask: why did the address shift from second person to third person in His words, "for her soul to the Prophet, if the Prophet wishes," and then return to the second person? I say: to signal that it is among what he was specially singled out for and given precedence; and its coming in the wording "the Prophet" serves to indicate that the singling out is an honour to him on account of prophethood; and repeating it is an exaltation of him and an affirmation of his deserving honour for his prophethood. Istinkahuha (marrying her in full) means seeking her in marriage and desiring it. Abu Hanifah cited this as evidence for the validity of a marriage contract with the wording of a gift (hibah), because the Messenger of God ﷺ and his community are equal in rulings except where a proof singles him out. Al-Shafi'i said: it is not valid; and the Prophet ﷺ was singled out in both the meaning and the wording of the gift, since wording follows meaning, and whoever claims sharing in the wording needs proof. Abu al-Hasan al-Karkhi said: a marriage contract with the wording of hire (ijarah) is valid, based on His words, "those whom you have given their dowries." Abu Bakr al-Razi said: it is not valid, because hire is a time-limited contract and marriage is perpetual, so the two are contradictory. Khalisah is an emphatic verbal noun, like "the promise of God" and "the dye of God," meaning: the lawfulness We have made for you is clearly yours, exclusive to you, as an exclusivity; and the agent noun and its feminine form are not rare in verbal nouns, like al-kharij and al-qa'id, and al-'afiyah and al-kadhibah. The evidence that they were revealed after the four lawful categories, specifically for the Messenger of God ﷺ, as an emphatic affirmation of them, is His words: "We know what We have decreed for them concerning their wives and what their right hands possess," after His words, "apart from the believers," and this is a parenthetical clause (jumlah i'tiradiyyah). His words, "so that there be no hardship upon you," are connected to "clearly yours, apart from the believers." The meaning of this parenthetical clause is that God knows what must be enjoined upon the believers regarding wives and slave-women, and to what extent and in what manner it must be enjoined upon them, so He enjoined it; and He knew the benefit in singling out the Messenger of God ﷺ with what He singled him out with, so He did it. "So that there be no hardship upon you" means: so that there be no constraint upon you in your religion, in that We have singled you out with purity and choosing what is more preferable and excellent; and in your worldly life, in that We have made lawful to you the kinds of women one may marry and added for you the woman who gives herself. It is read "khalisatan" in the accusative, meaning: that is a clear possession for you and a particularity apart from the believers. Whoever makes "khalisah" a qualifier of the woman, then on his view: this woman is exclusively yours apart from them. "And God is Forgiving" to the one who falls into hardship if he repents, "Merciful" in extending ease to His servants.

It is narrated that when the Mothers of the Believers became jealous of one another, sought an increase in maintenance, and vexed the Messenger of God ﷺ, he abandoned them for a month, and the choice (al-takhyir) was revealed; they feared he would divorce them, so they said: "O Messenger of God, impose upon us from yourself and your wealth whatever you wish." [This is a compilation of narrations. Its beginning, according to Muslim, through the route of Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir, who said: "Abu Bakr entered upon the Prophet ﷺ while people were sitting at the door... the hadith," and in it the saying of Abu Bakr and Umar; he said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ laughed and said: 'They are around me as you see, asking me for maintenance'—then he mentioned the hadith—and in it: 'So God revealed the verse of choice.'" And his saying, "he abandoned them for a month," is from the hadith of A'ishah in the two Sahihs. And his saying, "they feared he would divorce them—etc.," was narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah through the narration of Razin, that the Prophet ﷺ wished to part from his wives, and they said to him: "Apportion for us from yourself and your wealth whatever you wish, and leave us as we are." This is mursal. Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Salim al-Aftas from Mujahid, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ had nine wives, and they feared that he would divorce them, so they said: 'O Messenger of God, apportion for us from yourself and your wealth whatever you wish, and do not divorce us.' Then the verse was revealed: 'You may defer whom you will of them...'"]

It is narrated that A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, said: "O Messenger of God, I see your Lord hastening to fulfil your desire." [Agreed upon, from the hadith of Hisham from his father from A'ishah within a longer narration; al-Hakim erred and it was rectified by him.] "You may defer whom you will" — with hamz and without hamz — means: you may delay; "and take to yourself whom you will" means: you may join; that is: you may leave off lying with whom you will of them, and lie with whom you will. Or you may divorce whom you will and keep whom you will. Or you may not divorce, and you may apportion to whichever of them you will, and apportion to none; or you may leave off marrying whom you will of the women of your community, and marry whom you will. It is narrated from al-Hasan, may God be pleased with him: when the Prophet ﷺ proposed to a woman, no one was permitted to propose to her until he left her. This division is comprehensive of the purpose, for he either divorces or retains; if he retains, he lies with her or leaves her and apportions or does not apportion; and if he divorces and sets aside, then either he leaves the set-aside woman and does not seek her, or he seeks her. It is narrated that he deferred Sawdah, Juwayriyah, Safiyyah, Maymunah and Umm Habibah, and he apportioned to them whatever he willed, however he willed; and among those he took to himself were A'ishah, Hafsah, Umm Salamah and Zaynab, may God be pleased with them; he deferred five and took four to himself. [Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah from Jarir, and by Abd al-Razzaq from Ma'mar, both from Mansur from Abu Razin; this is mursal.] It is narrated that he would equalise among those whom he was permitted to not apportion among, and offered the choice to, except Sawdah, for she gave up her night to A'ishah and said: "Do not divorce me until I am raised in the company of your wives." [As for his equalising, it is from A'ishah's hadith, "he apportioned and was just." As for the story of Sawdah, al-Tirmidhi narrated from Ibn Abbas that "Sawdah feared the Messenger of God ﷺ would divorce her, so she said: 'O Messenger of God, do not divorce me; keep me, and give my day to A'ishah,' and he did so." In al-Tabarani, through the narration of Ibn Abi al-Zinad from Hisham from his father from A'ishah, she said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ did not prefer any of us over another in apportionment. Hardly a day passed without his circling us and approaching each of us without touching, until he reached the one whose day it was, and he would spend the night with her. Sawdah bint Zam'ah said to him, when he wished to part from her: 'My day is yours, and let me have A'ishah's.' He accepted this from her, and concerning her was revealed: 'And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion...'"]

"That delegation to your will is closer to comforting their eyes, to lessening their grief, and to all of them being content, because when he equalises among them in sheltering, deferring, setting aside and seeking, then distinction is removed, and none of them has in what she wants and what she does not want except the like of what the other has. When they know that this delegation is from God by His revelation, their souls are at rest, rivalry and jealousy depart, contentment is attained, eyes are comforted, and hearts are soothed." "And God knows what is in your hearts" — here is a warning to whoever among them is not content with what God has ordained and delegated to the will of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and an incitement to the harmony of their hearts, the purity of their relations with one another, and their agreement in seeking the pleasure of the Messenger of God ﷺ and that which brings contentment to his soul. It is read "tuqarra a'yunuhunna" with the tā' vowelled and the eyes in the accusative, and "taqarra a'yunuhunna" in the passive. "And God is All-Knowing of what is in the breasts, Forbearing" — who does not hasten punishment; so He is worthy to be feared and guarded against. "Kulluhunna" is an emphasis for the nūn of "yarḍayna" (they are content). Ibn Mas'ud read "wa-yarḍayna kulluhunna bi-mā ātaytahunna" with the object fronted. And [another] read "kulluhunna" as an emphasis for "hunna" in "ātaytahunna."
